 3 weather alerts in effect First Alert Weather: Flash flood warning extended for Kauai 
 Kuhio Highway remains closed at the Hanalei Bridge. Water was also rising rapidly along the south fork of the Wailua River. By Ben Gutierrez Published : Oct. 31, 2026 at 12:09 PM HST | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - The National Weather Service has extended a Flash Flood Warning for Kauai due to heavy rains occurring over the island. 
 The warning has been extended until 8:45 p.m. for the entire island.
 The National Weather Service in Honolulu said rain was falling at a rate of up 1 to 2 inches per hour. The heaviest rain was falling along the eastern slopes of Kauai, with more showers approaching from the southwest.
 Kuhio Highway remained closed at the Hanalei Bridge due to flooding. A rapid rise in water levels was also observed along the South Fork of the Wailua River. 
 A Flash Flood Warning means flash flooding is imminent or occurring in streams, roads and low-lying areas. Do not cross fast-flowing or rising water in your vehicle or on foot.
 Ponding, low visibility and other hazardous driving conditions are expected. If you must drive, please do so with extreme caution.
 For updates on road conditions and closures, call 808-241-1725. Do not call Kaua‘i police 911 unless you have an emergency.
 For weather updates call the National Weather Service automated weather line at 808-245-6001, or visit the NWS website, weather.gov/hfo .
 To sign up for Everbridge, the County’s emergency notification service, please visit kauai.gov/KEMA and click “Notification Services.” 
 You can also text “KAUAIEMA” to 888777, or call the Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency at 808-241-1800.
